A. History and Development of the Company
EZGO was incorporated in BVI on January 24, 2019.
EZGO’s wholly-owned subsidiary, EZGO HK, was incorporated in Hong Kong on February 13, 2019. EZGO HK holds all of the capital stock
of Changzhou EZGO, which was incorporated in China on June 12, 2019, and Changzhou Langyi, which was incorporated in China on August 6,
2021. EZGO is a holding company with no material operations of its own, and substantially all of its operations and assets are located
in China. EZGO conducts its business in China through its subsidiaries.
Beginning in November 2019, EZGO conducted a portion
of its business in China through VIE and the VIE’s subsidiaries. During this period, Changzhou EZGO controlled the VIE through a
series of contractual arrangements and EZGO was considered the primary beneficiary of the VIE for accounting purposes. As a result, EZGO
consolidated the financial results of the VIE and its subsidiaries under U.S. GAAP, even though neither EZGO nor its shareholders held
any equity ownership in the VIE. Through the VIE structure, EZGO engaged in the design, manufacture, rental and sale of e-bicycles and
e-tricycles, and in the sale, franchising and operation of smart charging piles for e-bicycles and other electronic devices.
On September 25, 2025, EZGO terminated the VIE
Agreements due to declined sales of e-bicycles. Following the termination of the VIE Agreements, EZGO no longer conducts any business
through a VIE structure, and its operations are carried out solely through its wholly-owned or controlled PRC subsidiaries.
After the termination of the VIE structure, EZGO’s
business is centered on its Internet of Things (“IoT”) product and service platform. EZGO has preliminarily established a
business model focused on electric vehicle accessories, including battery cells and packs and electronic control systems.
Recent Developments:
On February 18, 2025, the Board of Directors of
the Company approved and adopted an equity incentive plan (the “2025 Equity Incentive Plan”), which became effective on February
18, 2025. The 2025 Equity Incentive Plan authorizes the Company to issue up to 500,000 Ordinary Shares to its directors, officers, managers,
employees, consultants and advisors. On February 18, 2025, 500,000 restricted shares with 12-month service condition were granted to management
under the 2025 Equity Incentive Plan, which was issued on March 3, 2025 and shall vest after first anniversary of date of grant.
On July 30, 2025, Qixiang Liu resigned as a director
and as Chair of the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee and as a member of the Audit and Compensation Committees. Effective
July 31, 2025, the Board appointed Zhenguo Wu as a director and as Chair of the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee and a member
of the Audit and Compensation Committees.
Effective August 31, 2025, Jingyan Wu resigned
as Chief Financial Officer. Effective September 4, 2025, the Board appointed Yuehan Ling as Chief Financial Officer.
On August 27, 2025, the Company entered into a
warrant exchange agreement with certain holders of 5,389,126 outstanding warrants issued in September 2023. The holders agreed to cancel
these warrants in exchange for 1,246,000 Ordinary Shares and 10,879,534 pre-funded warrants, each exercisable for one Ordinary Share.
The pre-funded warrants carried a $0.04 exercise price, were immediately exercisable subject to beneficial ownership limits, and were
fully exercised as of the date of this filing. The securities issued in the exchange were made pursuant to Section 3(a)(9) of the Securities
Act.
On March 30, 2025, the Board approved the disposal
of the VIE and its subsidiaries due to declining e-bicycle sales, which met the held-for-sale criteria and resulted in discontinued operations
accounting under ASC 205-20-45. On September 25, 2025, Changzhou EZGO, the VIE and its shareholders entered into a termination agreement,
formally ending the VIE arrangements. Following this termination, the Company no longer has a VIE structure.
On October 1, 2025, the Board approved the October
2025 Equity Incentive Plan authorizing up to 3,400,000 Ordinary Shares (This amount does not give effect to the 1-for-25 reverse share
split that became effective on November 21, 2025). On October 2, 2025, the Company issued 3,400,000 Ordinary Shares under the plan to
WXYZ Group Ltd., an entity wholly owned by Mr. Jianhui Ye, the Company’s CEO and director, as compensation for his continued service.
The issuance was made pursuant to exemptions under Section 4(a)(2) and/or Regulation S of the Securities Act.
In November 2025, the Company’s
shareholders approved the 2025 Reverse Share Split and certain amendments to its authorized shares and memorandum and articles of
association which resulted in (a) an increase in the number of shares it is authorized to issue from
110,000,000 shares divided into up to 100,010,000 Ordinary Shares of US$0.04
each and up to 10,000 preferred shares of no par value each (b) a subsequent decrease in the number of shares it is authorized to
issue to 14,000,000 shares divided into up to 4,000,000 Ordinary Shares of US$1.00 each and up to 10,000 preferred shares of no par
value each and (c) a further increase in the number of shares it is authorized to issue to a maximum of 1,010,000,000 shares divided
into up to 1,000,000,000 Ordinary Shares (of no par value) each and 10,000,000 Preferred Shares (of no par value) each. Ordinary
Shares carry one vote per share and Preferred Shares carry 20 votes per share. The Company amended and restated its memorandum and
articles of association on November 6, 2025 to reflect these changes.
Minimum Bid Price Deficiency & Reverse
Split
On December 31, 2024, we announced that we received
written notification, or the Notification Letter, from Nasdaq on December 30, 2024 that we were not in compliance with the Minimum Bid
Price Requirement. In accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rules, we were required to regain compliance with the Minimum Bid Price Requirement
within 180 calendar days, or by June 30, 2025. On July 2, 2025, the Company received a letter from Nasdaq, indicating that the Company
is granted an additional 180 calendar days, until December 29, 2025, to regain compliance with the minimum bid price requirement of $1
per share, as stipulated by Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2).
On November 7, 2025, the Board of Directors
of EZGO approved a reverse share split (the “2025 Reverse Share Split”) of the Company’s Ordinary Shares at a
ratio of 1-for-25 so that every twenty-five (25) shares are combined into one (1) share (with the fractional shares rounding off to
the nearest whole share). The Company’s Ordinary Shares began trading on the Nasdaq Stock Market on a post-split basis on
November 21, 2025. Shortly after the 2025 Reverse Share Split, the par value of the Ordinary Shares of the Company was changed from
$0.04 per share to US$1.00 per share (as part of the 2025 Reverse Share Split) to no par value per share, and the Company’s
issued and outstanding Ordinary Shares was reduced from 21,700,706 to approximately 868,029.
On December 11, 2025, the Staff determined that,
for 13 consecutive business days, from November 21, 2025, through December 10, 2025, the closing bid price of the Company’s Ordinary
Shares has been at or above US$1.00 per share. Accordingly, the Company has regained compliance with Listing Rule 5550(a)(2), and Nasdaq
has confirmed that the matter is now closed.

B. Business Overview

BVI with operating subsidiaries in China. Historically, the Company conducted certain operations through the VIE structure; however, following

terminated the VIE Agreements on September 25, 2025. As of the date of this annual report, EZGO no longer maintains a VIE structure and
conducts its business solely through Changzhou EZGO and other wholly owned non-VIE subsidiaries in China.
